Credential precedence for Cloud commands:

1. `--api-key` — must be an
`sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.\n2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ign
ored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missing — Cloud comma
nds fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)\n\nAPI URL precedence:\

n
1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v1`)
3. The server saved with the OAu
th login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and on

e whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

Every command tha
t can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it contacts anythin
g. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a que
ry or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error masks credentials,
a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own server: when it is t
he credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same ch
ecks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.
valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\n\n
Successful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppress

es it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud commands pi

ck one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The

nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic — the most recently updated project you can see

Empty `--project` or `MCPJA
M_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a Cloud CLI project (it is SDK eval reporting only).\n\n```ba
sh theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\nmcpjam cloud login\nmcpjam cloud link # writes .mcpjam/project.json (no s
ecrets)\nmcpjam cloud status # zero-network: credential, deployment, selector\nmcpjam cloud eval list #

uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud eval` run-inspection commands (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iter
ations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `video`) follow the same rule — `--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud
sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-project listing and cannot be combined with `--project`. Hosted `readi

ness` never reads the project link.

## What `--host` means

`--host` is not one flag. The meaning depends on the command:
| Where | What it selects |\n| - | - |\n| `server`, `tools`, `resources`, `prompts` | An **AI client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `curs
or`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, and protocol version in `initialize`. |\n| `test --host` | One host
**template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, tool visibility and model settings. Never the real client. |\n| `co
mpat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default is all. |\n| `cloud eval --host`, `cloud goals`, `cloud studies` |
A **saved project Host** (`<id-or-name>`), the client config an eval or goal run is stamped with. |\n| `cloud environments --host-
id` | The project Host id the environment runs as. Distinct from eval's `--host`. |\n\n`--host` on a local command is mutually exc
lusive with `--client-capabilities`. A Cloud `--host` is mutually exclusive with `--server` / `--environment` when those already s

upply a closed server set.

## Global flags

These flags apply to every command. Cloud credentials `--api-key` / `--api-url` a

re declared on `mcpjam cloud`, not the program root.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--timeout <ms>` | `300
00` | Request timeout in milliseconds |\n| `--rpc` | off | Include raw JSON-RPC request/response logs in JSON output under `_rpcLo
gs` |\n| `--quiet` | off | Suppress non-result progress output on stderr |\n| `--no-telemetry` | off | Disable anonymous telemetry
for this invocation |\n| `--format <format>` | `human` on TTY, `json` when piped | Raw output format (`json` or `human`) |\n| `-v

, --version` | | Print the CLI version |

## Output formats

The CLI auto-detects whether stdout is a terminal:

* **Interac
tive terminal** — defaults to `--format human`. For most commands this is pretty-printed JSON; `server doctor` and the OAuth confo
rmance commands provide dedicated human-readable summaries.\n* **Piped or redirected** (CI, `| jq`, agent invocation) — defaults t
o `--format json`, the full structured result.\n* **Conformance in CI** — `protocol conformance`, `protocol conformance-suite`, `o
auth conformance`, `oauth conformance-suite`, `apps conformance`, and `apps conformance-suite` support `--reporter junit-xml` and

`--reporter json-summary`.
* **Explicit `--format`** always wins over the auto-detected default.

**For agents**: raw JSON is t
he source of truth. Human format is a lossy presentation layer. If you're parsing output programmatically, pass `--quiet --format
json`.\n\nJSON-valued flags accept inline JSON, `@path`, or `-` for stdin. `tools call` also accepts `--tool-args-stdin` as a shor
thand for `--tool-args -`. Use files or stdin for large payloads to avoid shell escaping issues:\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css
-variables\"}\necho '{\"key\":\"value\"}' | mcpjam tools call --url $URL --access-token $TOKEN \\\n --tool-name my_tool --tool-ar

gs - --quiet --format json
```

## Connecting to servers

The CLI supports two transport modes, selected by which flags you p

ass:

* `--url ...` selects HTTP.
* `--command ...` selects stdio.
* `--transport http|stdio` is optional and acts as an expli

cit override/validator when you want the CLI to reject mismatched flags early.

### HTTP (Streamable HTTP / SSE)

```bash them

e={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp
```

Add auth when needed:

```bash t
heme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\n# Static bearer token\nmcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $

TOKEN

# OAuth tokens from a prior login
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# Custom headers
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

### Stdio (local sub

ct -e API_KEY=[REDACTED]
```

Stdio child processes inherit the parent shell environment by default. Use
`-e/--env` to add val
ues or override inherited ones for the spawned server.\nStructured debug artifacts only record the explicit env keys you pass thro

ugh
`-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerated.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `oauth ...` and `protocol ...` are HTTP-only com

mand groups. They do
> not accept stdio targets.

## Update notifications

After a successful command, the CLI checks whether

a newer version of `@mcpjam/cli` is available and prints a notice to stderr when one is found:

```
Update available: @mcpjam/

cli 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0
Run npm install -g @mcpjam/cli to update
```

The check is non-blocking: version data is fetched in a detac
hed background process and cached locally for 24 hours, so it never slows down your commands. The notice is written to stderr only
and never touches stdout or JSON output, so it is safe for both interactive terminals and AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) t
hat capture stderr. It is suppressed automatically in CI.\n\nTo opt out, set one of these environment variables before running any

command:

| Variable | Effect |
| - | - |
| `MCPJAM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` | Disable update checks for `@mcpjam/cli` |
| `NO_UPD
